title: Translate postmortem actions into PRD: Degradation agreements and operational checklist
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: After the kv-cache coldstart incident (2026-02-26) the SRE and runtime teams produced a postmortem with action items to formalize how degraded serving is allowed, detected, and remediated. This ticket translates those actions into explicit PRD updates: a "degradation agreements" section that codifies acceptable SLO reductions and compensation windows, an "operational checklist" for on-call and release engineers, and required acceptance tests (deterministic degraded-path simulations and synthetic verification). The goal is to make rollback/mitigation decisions unambiguous and automatable for runtime and Dedicated/Private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: PRD updated with a new Degradation Agreements section that lists measurable thresholds for SLO reduction, max duration per incident, and customer communication triggers
Operational checklist appended to PRD with step-by-step runbook for on-call including circuit-breaker toggles, fallback model variants, and capacity re-routing

Define deterministic degraded-mode tests and add at least three automated synthetic scenarios that reproduce the postmortem failure modes (kv cache coldstart, autoscale lag, regional routing fallback)
Add release gates that require passing degradation-mode chaos runs to merge runtime rollout changes (documented in PRD)
Assign owners for each runbook task and include escalation SLA (e.g., 15m ack, 60m mitigation action) in PRD
Include monitoring and dashboard requirements: token-level latency histogram, degraded-path counts, and automated alerts wired to on-call
decisions: Scope change: PRD will require explicit degradation policies for hosted, dedicated, and private deployments rather than a single global statement
Acceptance tests will run in a separate staging cluster using traffic shaping to avoid impacting production
Fallbacks: prefer model-variant fallbacks before cross-region failover to reduce customer impact
Owners: Runtime team owns testing harness; SRE owns alert definitions and on-call checklist; PM maintains PRD and runs quarterly review
unresolved_questions: Should compensation/credits be automated based on degradation duration or handled case-by-case by customer success?
What level of granularity should be required for per-tenant degradation agreements in Dedicated customers?
Do we need an API-level signal to mark traffic as 'degraded' so customers can programmatically handle lower-quality responses?
